items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: my debut recording with him... I was sent to Jackie McLean... he says, 'Okay I’m putting you on my next record date.'

ctx.x: I do. I think that’s why Ellington kept his band together for so long, right? That is an interesting observation. I had a quote here about both your composing and your playing. It comes from one of those Jazz on CD books. And this particular reviewer made the observation that most of your compositions instead of complex chords, I think he’s referring to like bebop, “Charles favors basic motifs, four or five notes in an ostinato,” and then he continued, “it’s very much harder to play inventively over such a…

Well you know I wouldn’t be where I am today, you know, in this art form, had it not been for Jackie McLean. That’s what I’m talking about, that lucky break you know. And my first, my debut recording with him, as you know, Jackie was a dye-in-the-wool, you know, bebopper. But that was, I came in during that generational shift just as you know the freer forms were being used. I mean he was already, he had already done “Destination Out” and a couple of other things which portend that he, you know, he wasn’t just…

thing. And he wanted something a little bit different. And so you know like half of that recording is bebop and half of it is what you are talking about. And from that experience I think is where I started to do those sorts of things that this person observed in my work. But I think Andrew Hill is the one who really, once I started playing with Andrew and recording with him, you know, that sort of thing really became also a part of my delivery process.
